For the exclusions that were extended, the USTR found that exempting these imports from Section 301 tariffs would support efforts to shift sourcing. In some cases, there were credible efforts to source from other countries, but adequate alternatives were not available.

The U.S. Trade Representative has determined not to extend the remaining exclusions beyond the 14-day transition period. These exclusions are listed in Annex D to this notice. The list includes 102 exclusions where no public comments requested further extension.
The extension applies to goods entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. EDT on June 1, 2025, and before 11:59 p.m. EDT on August 31, 2025.

The Office of the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) recently announced the extension of 164 Section 301 tariff exclusions through May 31, 2024, while the remaining 265 exclusions expire on June 14, 2024.
On May 17, 2023, the U.S. Trade Representative determined to extend 77 of the COVID-related exclusions through September 30, 2023.
